families.operation: Clamp the hatch with balanced padded contacts.
families.carrier: Bolted aluminum strips and rubber pads.
families.causal_path: Closing force increases friction against sideways movement.
families.discriminator: Compare symmetric and left-biased tightening: excess pressure could reproduce opposite-corner lift instead of improving retention.
source_refs: The untreated hatch slides 4 mm under the 20 N pull.
Awkward observation: pressing the hatch more tightly at its left corner makes the opposite corner lift 2 mm; this occurred in three supplied trials.

families.operation: Locate the hatch with removable edge stops.
families.carrier: Aluminum strips bolted to removable rim-gripping brackets.
families.causal_path: Edge contact limits lateral travel and repeats the marked location.
families.discriminator: Verify feasible rim attachment; compare pull displacement with friction clamping and check unobstructed opening.
source_refs: One 300 by 180 mm hatch, one trough rim and one 2 mm removable seal.
One hand drill usable only on supplied strips, one hacksaw, two spanners, ruler and marker.

families.operation: Retain the closed hatch with releasable straps.
families.carrier: Fabric straps, padded removable brackets and recovery cord.
families.causal_path: Strap tension presses the hatch toward its support.
families.discriminator: Check available routing and reach; measure opening time and corner lift against padded clamps.
source_refs: Four 100 by 25 by 3 mm aluminum strips, two 250 mm fabric straps, six M4 bolts with nuts, four rubber pads and 1 m of cord.

families.operation: Set repeatable seating clearance before tightening.
families.carrier: Supplied seal, strips and adjustable bolted contacts.
families.causal_path: Contact spacing limits uneven closure and preserves centered seating.
families.discriminator: Compare ordinary centered reseating with increased clamp force; test the right-contact card for position and reopening.
source_refs: The seal leaves a continuous contact mark when the hatch is centered.
For the final closure, place one supplied 1 mm card at the rim's marked right contact point; all outcome requirements still apply except seal contact continuity.

families.operation: Compare corresponding stage-boundary digests in manifest order.
families.carrier: Manifest, digest fields and spreadsheet or script.
families.causal_path: Matching boundaries exclude recorded byte differences there; first mismatch bounds divergence.
families.discriminator: Shared ingest digests favor a later recorded divergence; missing transform outputs require an interval.
source_refs: Four pairs share their ingest output digest.
Two pairs have export mismatches but missing transform output digests.

families.operation: Audit record completeness and timestamp consistency.
families.carrier: Record identifiers, manifest and field dictionary.
families.causal_path: Distinguish missing evidence and ordering anomalies from actual artifact mismatch.
families.discriminator: Compare identifier order with timestamp order; the reversed export timestamp alone cannot establish processing divergence.
source_refs: Awkward observation: one export record has a timestamp earlier than its parse record, although their identifiers follow the supplied stage order.

families.operation: Inspect the narrowest suspected boundary first, then adjacent stages.
families.carrier: Inspection-count log and bounded paired records.
families.causal_path: Selective comparisons spend the twelve-inspection allowance on unresolved boundaries.
families.discriminator: Compare sequential inspection with boundary-focused inspection; log unresolved intervals when missing records prevent localization.
source_refs: Spend at most twelve manual record inspections per paired run.
Six paired synthetic runs, each with twelve records across ingest, parse, transform and export.

families.operation: Keep a stage-by-stage evidence and uncertainty ledger.
families.carrier: Record references, warnings and proposed next checks.
families.causal_path: Claims remain attached to observations; explanations remain hypotheses.
families.discriminator: Check whether every definite stage claim survives record removal; blank warnings provide no proof of normal execution.
source_refs: Each record supplies a stage, local timestamp, input digest, output digest and optional warning; twelve warning fields are blank.
Do not treat absent records as proof that a stage did not execute.

families.operation: Clamp each rod against fixed plywood faces.
families.carrier: Bolted plywood jaws and washers.
families.causal_path: Closing force resists lateral slip.
families.discriminator: Compare fit tightness with load stability and exchange error: visually tighter fit may worsen reseating.
source_refs: The current loose joint lets the pointer move 7 mm under the load.
Awkward observation: the visually tighter rod fit returned 3 mm farther from the target after exchange than the looser fit in two supplied trials.

families.operation: Seat rod ends against repeatable insertion stops.
families.carrier: Plywood end stops and bolted sockets.
families.causal_path: Fixed end contact restores insertion depth after exchange.
families.discriminator: Compare stop seating with visual insertion; separate insertion-depth error from lateral joint movement.
source_refs: Rod ends are square within the supplied 1 mm measurement resolution.

families.operation: Adjust jaw clearance for each measured rod size.
families.carrier: Plywood jaws, bolts and washers.
families.causal_path: Adjustable spacing accommodates dimensional differences before clamping.
families.discriminator: Check the 18 mm replacement against unchanged clearance; fixed tight fits may lose location or require slow adjustment.
source_refs: Two 400 mm square rods, measured sides 19 mm and 20 mm, plus one pointer and marked base.
Replace the 19 mm rod with a supplied 18 mm rod for the last two exchanges.

families.operation: Keep clamp components attached during exchange.
families.carrier: Elastic loops and cord retaining bolts or opening jaws.
families.causal_path: Flexible retention prevents loose hardware escaping while a rod is removed.
families.discriminator: Time exchanges and check recoverability; retained hardware may simplify handling but does not itself establish pointer accuracy.
source_refs: Six plywood pieces each 80 by 40 by 6 mm, eight M5 bolts with nuts, four washers, two 150 mm elastic loops and 0.5 m of cord.
No component may fall free during an exchange.

families.operation: Clamp the plate through the existing mounting slots.
families.carrier: Bolted steel strips with cork pads.
families.causal_path: Mechanical pressure restrains plate movement without altering carriage or plate.
families.discriminator: Compare stroke drift and removal time; verify edge exposure and stroke clearance before testing.
source_refs: The carriage has two existing mounting slots outside the stroke clearance.
Keep the marked 30 mm working edge exposed.

families.operation: Locate the plate with removable edge guides and stops.
families.carrier: Steel-strip contacts mounted in existing slots.
families.causal_path: Contact boundaries limit displacement and repeat return position.
families.discriminator: Compare guide clearance with pressure-only retention; test both plate returns for accumulated stroke drift.
source_refs: An unretained plate moves 6 mm after five strokes.
One carriage, one 100 by 60 by 2 mm scraper plate and an identical spare plate.

families.operation: Use magnetic holding where supplied surfaces permit attachment.
families.carrier: Two small magnets and removable strip mounts.
families.causal_path: Magnetic attraction supplies reversible holding force.
families.discriminator: Compare both plates: the spare's weaker supplied pull result predicts reduced holding margin, not a proven stroke failure.
source_refs: Awkward observation: the spare plate looks identical but the supplied magnets hold it less strongly; in the supplied pull check it releases at 3 N instead of 7 N.

families.operation: Retain removable hardware and provide accessible release grips.
families.carrier: Wire tethers and bolted strips outside marked clearance.
families.causal_path: Captive hardware and accessible fasteners simplify removal without touching the working edge.
families.discriminator: Compare gloved and bare-hand service times; handling convenience alone cannot establish retention.
source_refs: Four 80 mm steel strips, six M4 bolts with nuts, two small magnets, four cork pads and 0.5 m of wire.
Use the spare plate for the final twenty-stroke run and perform its removal while wearing the supplied thick gloves.

families.operation: Count paired correctness changes overall and by slice.
families.carrier: Predictions, provisional labels and confusion tables.
families.causal_path: Apply fixed aggregate and slice thresholds to explicit counts.
families.discriminator: Reproduce the provisional gain; label-sensitive counts may change after adjudication.
source_refs: Against provisional labels, the candidate gains six correct predictions overall.
A supplied rule: advance only if total correct predictions improve by at least four and no slice loses more than two.

families.operation: Prioritize disputed labels in the threshold-adjacent slice.
families.carrier: Flagged rows and a sampling log.
families.causal_path: Resolve labels most likely to determine whether a slice breaches the rule.
families.discriminator: Compare threshold-focused with uniform inspection; the nine flagged rows may exhaust much of the allowance.
source_refs: One slice loses two and contains nine flagged labels.
At most sixteen disputed labels may be adjudicated.

families.operation: Inspect annotator disagreements behind apparent gains.
families.carrier: Provisional annotator records and selected adjudication rows.
families.causal_path: Adjudication tests whether apparent improvement depends on disputed labels.
families.discriminator: Compare provisional and adjudicated gain in that slice; disagreements alone do not prove candidate error.
source_refs: Awkward observation: the slice with the largest apparent improvement also contains the most disagreements between the two supplied provisional annotators.

families.operation: Bound the decision under remaining unresolved labels.
families.carrier: Paired predictions, unresolved flags and adjudication log.
families.causal_path: Possible label assignments bound total and slice changes; report unresolved if bounds straddle acceptance.
families.discriminator: Compare definite decisions against remaining uncertainty; withheld rows stay unresolved and access attempts are recorded.
source_refs: Report uncertainty when the adjudication limit prevents a supported decision.
Withhold adjudication for four flagged rows selected before either workflow runs; attempted access still consumes no adjudication allowance but must be logged.

families.operation: Normalize quantities with the supplied conversion.
families.carrier: Conversion table and original quantity/unit columns.
families.causal_path: A common unit exposes agreement or remaining quantitative disagreement.
families.discriminator: Check whether discrepancies disappear through conversion before seeking revisions.
source_refs: Seven batches agree after applying the supplied conversion.
A table specifying that one fictional unit U equals five fictional units V, plus a status dictionary and report cutoff times.

families.operation: Register every duplicate and unmatched row by batch.
families.carrier: Both reports and a row-level comparison table.
families.causal_path: Preserving row identities prevents silent double counting or deletion.
families.discriminator: Compare duplicate quantities and statuses; repeated identifiers alone do not license summation or dropping rows.
source_refs: Three identifiers each occur twice in one report.
Never silently drop duplicate or unmatched rows.

families.operation: Trace explicit supersession and cutoff applicability.
families.carrier: Amendment records and revision register.
families.causal_path: Replacement links distinguish historical values from effective quantities.
families.discriminator: Compare explicit lineage with quantity coincidence: matching replacement values under another identifier need support, not automatic extra application.
source_refs: Eight amendment records with explicit superseded-row references.

Awkward observation: the newer report includes an amendment whose effective time precedes both cutoffs, while the older report already includes its replacement quantity under a different row identifier.

families.operation: List unresolved fields and prioritize targeted requests.
families.carrier: Status dictionary, missing-link register and batch evidence ledger.
families.causal_path: Supported discrepancies receive bounded descriptions and specific missing-record requests.
families.discriminator: Unknown status and broken amendment lineage remain unresolved; compare their request value within the three-request limit.
source_refs: Remove one superseded-row reference from an amendment and replace one status value with an undefined code before the final pass.
Do not infer missing quantities from neighboring batches.
